articles.title: High Availability by Offloading Work Into the Background
articles.read_scope: Complete main narrative, including Background Jobs, Challenges, Long Running Jobs and conclusion; linked talks not watched.

practice.failure: Every interruption restarts work before it can finish; queued arguments can outlive their producing binary.
practice.mechanism: Interrupt at iteration boundaries, preserve the cursor, and maintain compatible job arguments across rollout.
practice.conditions: An iteration fits the shutdown budget and the queue adapter preserves continuation state.
practice.limits: This does not make external effects atomic with checkpoint publication or ensure immutable input.
practice.counterexample: A non-idempotent effect completes and the process dies before the cursor is persisted.
practice.verification: Repeat planned interruptions, verify monotonic durable progress, then kill at the effect/checkpoint boundary and reconcile the original operation identity.

proposed_change.classification: Article corroborates existing general rules; current framework guide adds a conditional runtime gap
proposed_change.gap: For job-iteration, distinguish Active Job retry continuation from unsupported backend-level retry fallback.

articles.limitations: Historical operational account; no Shopify system, Ruby runtime, or linked sample was executed. Broad unrelated saga/Kafka claims were not adopted.

articles.title: Announcing Amazon ECS Task Scale-in protection
articles.read_scope: Complete main narrative, queue-consumer sample and WebSocket example; code and logs read, not copied or executed.

practice.trigger: An ECS service scales down or deploys while workers process long tasks.
practice.failure: The scheduler cannot infer outstanding work; interruption loses progress and redelivery may spend an independent delivery budget.
practice.mechanism: Acquire protection before queue receive; release after work finishes, accounting for every concurrent work unit.
practice.conditions: Service-managed ECS tasks, acknowledged protection, sufficient lifetime and replacement capacity.
practice.limits: Protection and queue acceptance are separate operations; coverage is service-autoscaling/deployment scale-in, not all termination causes.
practice.counterexample: The worker continues polling after acquisition fails or a renewal expires.
practice.verification: Inject acquisition and renewal failure, overlap completions, and block replacement capacity; assert bounded recoverable disposition.

proposed_change.gap: Protection lifecycle and live old-revision retirement evidence are not described in the existing platform reference.

articles.limitations: No ECS service created. Historical sample does not establish a 24-hour retention guarantee, atomic receive/protect, or survival of crashes/host interruption.

articles.publisher: AWS Blu Insights (page now branded AWS Transform for mainframe refactor)
articles.title: AWS Blu Insights - Scaling out/in policies and task protection in practice
articles.date_precision: month; no day or named author shown
articles.access: Public full HTML article on first-party .aws domain with Amazon Web Services copyright
articles.read_scope: Complete main narrative, scale policies, active-work protection manager, remaining deactivation race and custom scale-in design; diagrams not independently reconstructed.

practice.trigger: Scale-in overlaps the transition from idle/unprotected to receiving work.
practice.failure: Long requests arriving while a task deactivates outlast its remaining lifetime and fail.
practice.mechanism: Track active work and protection renewal; test admission against the complete retirement transition.
practice.conditions: Actual routing convergence and task lifecycle must be observed in the selected platform.
practice.limits: The account does not prove its custom scaler atomically retires exactly the chosen targets.
practice.counterexample: An earlier asynchronous unprotect request arrives after fresh work is admitted; this schedule is our inferred risk, not an incident reported by the article.
practice.verification: Delay release, attempt admission, and require explicit ordering or closed admission with recoverable work.

proposed_change.classification: Existing admission rule corroborated; asynchronous protection-transition test is a new refinement
proposed_change.gap: Do not confuse observed idle state, a pending unprotect request, and completed admission closure.

articles.limitations: Historical latency and scaling thresholds are not defaults. Its broad full-deregistration-delay claim conflicts with current ALB documentation and is excluded.

runtime_sources.title: Protect your Amazon ECS tasks from being terminated by scale-in events
runtime_sources.version_or_pin: Latest documentation accessed 2026-09-29; ECS agent requirement documented as 1.65.0 or later
runtime_sources.read_scope: Overview, mechanisms, considerations and IAM permissions
runtime_sources.findings: Applies to service-managed tasks. Protection can block old-task cleanup and deployment progress; inspect maximumPercentage, capacity, tool timeouts and DEPLOYMENT_BLOCKED. Renewal resets a finite expiry. Current early-success documentation must be considered before generalizing historical deployment-timeout advice.

runtime_sources.title: Amazon ECS task scale-in protection endpoint
runtime_sources.read_scope: Request parameters, response state, failure and error bodies
runtime_sources.findings: Protection lasts 1–2,880 minutes, default 120. The stated coverage is service-autoscaling/deployment scale-in. Inspect ProtectionEnabled, ExpirationDate and task identity; timeout, access and throttling errors are documented. A successful transport operation alone is insufficient admission evidence.

runtime_sources.title: UpdateTaskProtection
runtime_sources.read_scope: Request syntax and parameters, response elements and errors
runtime_sources.findings: The response separates protectedTasks from failures; inspect per-task results.

runtime_sources.title: Amazon ECS API failure reasons
runtime_sources.findings: TASK_NOT_VALID denotes a task not belonging to an ECS service. DEPLOYMENT_BLOCKED denotes protection preventing deployment stabilization. No exact already-stopping-task rejection code was verified.

runtime_sources.title: Amazon ECS clusters for Fargate: Fargate Spot termination notices
runtime_sources.read_scope: Capacity-provider overview and Spot termination notices
runtime_sources.findings: Fargate Spot requires interruption-tolerant work and documents a two-minute warning. It does not promise a task-protection exception. Excluding Spot survival from the narrower scale-in guarantee is a conservative inference.

runtime_sources.title: StopTask
runtime_sources.read_scope: Operation behavior, stop signal and configurable timeout note; response schema not analyzed
runtime_sources.findings: Explicit stop sends the container stop signal, followed by forceful termination when its timeout elapses. This page does not promise a task-protection exception; do not include manual stops in the narrower protection guarantee.

runtime_sources.title: HealthCheck
runtime_sources.findings: An unhealthy service-managed task is stopped and replaced. This page does not promise a task-protection exception; retaining recovery for that cause is a conservative interpretation of the protection scope.

runtime_sources.title: Complete Amazon ECS rolling deployments early with early success criteria
runtime_sources.version_or_pin: Rolling strategy, earlySuccessCriteria; accessed 2026-09-29, selected project SDK/IaC support untested
runtime_sources.read_scope: Healthy percent, cleanup ordering, observations and considerations; configuration example read only
runtime_sources.findings: DEFERRED permits successful deployment before source cleanup. Cleanup is attempted for up to two weeks. Deployment rollback monitoring ends at completion. Completed DescribeServiceDeployments counts are snapshots; DescribeServices provides live service counts.

runtime_sources.title: Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer: Deregistration delay
runtime_sources.read_scope: Deregistration-delay behavior and configuration section only
runtime_sources.findings: No active connections or in-flight requests permits immediate completed deregistration even while the displayed status remains draining. Premature connection closure can produce a 500-level response.

runtime_sources.title: Shopify job-iteration README
runtime_sources.version_or_pin: Commit c3b0eb1db5bd6681664913d57dfe5b5b28ab2ad8, HEAD resolved with git ls-remote on 2026-09-29; not asserted to be an installed release
runtime_sources.read_scope: Complete README including supported adapters, configuration and interruption/retry FAQ
runtime_sources.findings: Documents interruption separately from exception retry and resumes from a serialized cursor. Actual iteration timeout depends on the queue adapter; the README's rough 30-second recommendation is not a universal safe bound.

runtime_sources.title: Iteration: how it works
runtime_sources.read_scope: Complete guide, especially exceptions and signals
runtime_sources.findings: Configure Active Job retries for continuation. Backend-level retries are documented as unsupported and restarting at the beginning. A deterministic failing iteration can exhaust retries without reaching later items.

runtime_sources.title: Job Iteration best practices
runtime_sources.read_scope: Complete guide; batch, instrumentation and runtime sections
runtime_sources.findings: Distinguishes batch loading from the interruptible work unit. Provides interruption/progress instrumentation and optional periodic yielding for capacity. Its specific internal time limits are examples, not adopted defaults.

runtime_sources.title: JobIteration::Iteration implementation
runtime_sources.read_scope: Serialization/deserialization, iteration callback/cursor ordering, interruption and re-enqueue functions; remaining file scanned
runtime_sources.findings: Cursor assignment follows each iteration callback; serialization includes cursor_position, times_interrupted and total_time. Re-enqueue increments the separate interruption counter. This code does not couple an arbitrary external effect atomically to cursor persistence.

runtime_sources.title: Sidekiq Deployment
runtime_sources.version_or_pin: Current wiki accessed 2026-09-29; installed Sidekiq version not tested
runtime_sources.read_scope: Deployment overview, TSTP/TERM order and timeout guidance
runtime_sources.findings: TSTP stops fetching early, TERM starts bounded shutdown (default timeout 25 seconds). The guide requires timeout plus five seconds before external KILL; early KILL can lose work or cause duplicates depending on fetch implementation.

proposed_acceptance.scenario: Protection acquisition is denied, times out, returns a failure body, or renewal is lost near expiry.
proposed_acceptance.pass: No new work is admitted without confirmed coverage; accepted or racing receipts retain logical identity and follow an explicit bounded recovery path. Independent broker limits remain visible.

proposed_acceptance.scenario: Delay a release while another work unit attempts admission; overlap two active work units and complete one.
proposed_acceptance.pass: Protection is not released while work remains. A retiring process never reopens admission. Reusable idle-worker admission waits for ordered, resolved transitions; unresolved remote ordering is reported rather than hidden by a local boolean.

proposed_acceptance.scenario: All old workers are protected and replacement capacity or maximumPercentage prevents progress.
proposed_acceptance.pass: Report a bounded deployment block and a reviewed finish-or-resume decision; do not discard accepted work merely to clear deployment status.

proposed_acceptance.scenario: DEFERRED rollout reports SUCCESSFUL while old tasks retain nonterminal jobs.
proposed_acceptance.pass: Retirement remains incomplete; use live task/job inventory, retained dependencies, a cleanup deadline and an explicit post-completion recovery owner. Snapshot deployment counts cannot close the gate.

proposed_acceptance.scenario: Three planned handoffs, a configured Active Job exception retry, backend retry fallback, and abrupt death after an effect before re-enqueue.
proposed_acceptance.pass: Observe progress and each counter layer. Planned continuation preserves the logical failure budget; unsupported fallback exposes restart behavior. Replayed effects use stable identity or reconciliation, and old/new inputs remain compatible.

not_adopted: A universal 24-hour shutdown grace or protection against every ECS termination cause.
The assumption that ECS protection and queue receive form one atomic claim.
Blu Insights' workload-specific scale thresholds or an unverified custom scaler protocol.
A universal full deregistration-delay wait inferred from the ALB draining display state.
A default 30-second iteration independent of the real adapter shutdown budget.
General saga, Kafka or infinite buffering claims outside this worker-rollout scope.

execution_evidence.existing_fixture_scope: The previously validated PostgreSQL/process draining fixture remains separate evidence; this extension does not expand its platform or duration claims.

independent_crosscheck.scope: Current protection scope and errors, separate termination contracts, DEFERRED completion versus retirement
independent_crosscheck.result: Confirmed narrow scope and retirement distinction; corrected against attributing TASK_NOT_VALID to an already-stopping task. No cloud operations or runtime reproduction.
